criterion: Happy-path-only (Meszaros): no off-boundary/negative cases around new comparisons
finding: Likely weak coverage: the delta adds three refusal guards to the main-checkout read (repository root equals $HOME, an entry not owned by the user, a common dir not ending in /.git), and no test drives any of them. Deleting line 93 or the loop at 94-96 would leave the suite green.
why: PROVIDERS.md now documents these guards as harness behaviour the check mirrors. The only worktree test sets HOME to a directory that does not exist (fixture `HOME=str(tmp_path / "nohome")`), so line 92 yields an empty `home` and line 93 can never fire. Every tmp_path entry is user-owned, so `[ -O ]` is always true. Checked by reading: no test in scripts/tests/test_team_permission.py sets HOME to the main checkout, and none makes a common dir that does not end in /.git (grep of the file for `HOME`, `chown`, `--separate-git-dir`: only the fixture line).
fix: Off Windows, add a case: the linked-worktree setup with HOME pointed at `main`, asserting `files` omits the main local file and the answer is `missing`. Add a case with `git init --separate-git-dir` (common dir not ending in /.git), asserting the same. Leave ownership to a documented skip, or stub `[ -O` through a shim, if a non-owned fixture is impractical.
evidence: claude.sh:93 `[ -n "$home" ] && [ "$(cd "$top" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" = "$home" ] && return 0`; claude.sh:95 `[ ! -e "$entry" ] || [ -O "$entry" ] || return 0`; test_team_permission.py:53 `HOME=str(tmp_path / "nohome")`

criterion: documented behaviour matches the code's refusal condition
finding:
PROVIDERS.md says a detected provider that prints a rule refuses when its adapter "does not define the other two" functions. The adapter script refuses when either one is missing: it checks `afk_

_spawn_rule_files` and `afk_

_spawn_rule_lists` one at a time and exits 3 at the first one it cannot find. Read literally, the doc says an adapter missing only one of the two answers ok, and the code does not do that.
why: A harness author who follows the doc may define only one of the two functions and expect an ok. Instead they get a provider-layer refusal on every team run.
fix: Change the clause to "or prints a rule and does not define either of the other two" (or "is missing `afk_<name>_spawn_rule_files` or `afk_<name>_spawn_rule_lists`").
evidence: PROVIDERS.md:188 "A detected provider whose adapter does not define that function, or prints a rule and does not define the other two, refuses with `provider-layer`" vs scripts/team/permission.py:41-42 "need \"afk_${p}_spawn_rule_files\"" / "need \"afk_${p}_spawn_rule_lists\"" where :36 "need() { command -v \"$1\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf 'undefined\t%s\n' \"$1\"; exit 3; }; }"

criterion: caller whose contract the diff changed but did not update
finding: The delta sends every provider-layer refusal to /afk:setup and adds a new one (an adapter without a spawn function, D-79). But the H15 row in /afk:setup, which runs this check as its probe, was not updated. Its Probe text still promises that every refusal names the rule, the settings file and the list. Its Fix (print `rule --json`, wait for the human to add the entry, probe again) cannot clear a provider-layer refusal: `rule` exits 1 on that path, and the refusal tells a setup run to run /afk:setup.
why: The one in-tree consumer of the refusal set (skills/afk/setup/MANIFEST.md H15, in Scope) now describes a refusal shape the delta no longer guarantees. On a provider-layer refusal the human gets a fix loop that cannot end. The path is reachable today through a bash failure or timeout; the D-79 path is not reachable yet.
fix: Add one clause to H15's Probe or Notes: a `provider-layer` refusal is a plugin defect, not a missing entry. Report its `says` and stop the row (no rule print, no wait loop).

Wait until the human says it is added, then probe again (step 5).`

criterion: Conditional test logic (Meszaros): a platform branch steers the asserts
finding: Possible conditional test logic: one test picks its expected answer from `_windows_shell()`. On Windows it passes after proving only the skip branch, and nothing reports that the positive read of the main-checkout file went unproven.
why: On a Windows run (this machine's `uname -s` is MINGW64_NT-10.0-26200), the test name claims both behaviours but proves only one, and the result shows as passed, not skipped. The branch does catch a regression on Windows: I ran the adapter's own probes here, all three entries are user-owned, and the git common dir ends in /.git, so without line 88 the file would be listed and the test would fail.
fix: Split it into two tests over a shared worktree fixture: one marked `skipif(not windows_shell)` that asserts `missing` with no files, and one marked `skipif(windows_shell)` that asserts ok with exactly the main local file.
evidence: test_team_permission.py:120 `expected = "missing" if _windows_shell() else None`; :121 `assert answer["problem"] == expected and answer["ok"] is (expected is None)`

finding:
The test for a harness missing its functions covers `need` for the allow-rule function and for the rule-files function, but not the third `need`, for `afk_

_spawn_rule_lists`. It also never asserts that this refusal keeps the rule the adapter printed.
why: If someone deleted `need "afk_${p}_spawn_rule_lists"` (permission.py:42), no test would fail. An adapter that defines the files function but not the lists function would then print files with no lists, and the check would fall through to `missing` instead of `provider-layer`. That breaks D-79 and PROVIDERS.md ("prints a rule and does not define the other two, refuses with `provider-layer`"). The kept-rule change at permission.py:58 is proven only through the fake runner, never through a real undefined-function refusal.
fix: Add a third parametrize row whose adapter defines `afk_newharness_spawn_allow_rule` and `afk_newharness_spawn_rule_files` but not `_rule_lists`, expecting `afk_newharness_spawn_rule_lists`. In the rows that print `Bash(x *)`, assert `answer["rule"] == "Bash(x *)"`.
